METERS IN SY.NO.47/2 OF BIDRAHALLI HOBLI, BHATTARAHALLI VILLAGE K R PURAM TALUK, BENGALURU EAST IN TERMS OF THE FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 14.11.2007 ANNEXURE-G AND ETC.

THIS WRIT PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -5-  NC: 2023:KHC:28594  WP No. 4591 of 2022  ORDER R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
Learned Counsel for the respondent-National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)
submits that the connected writ petitions filed at the hands of few other persons, who are claiming along with the petitioner has been disposed of in W.P.No.47131/2015, by order dated 01.08.2023.
2.
Accepting the submission of the learned Counsel for the respondent-NHAI this Court held that the redetermination of the award cannot be done by this Court in writ proceedings.
Provision is made under the Act in sub-section (5) of Section 3G of National Highways Act, 1956, enabling the dissatisfied parties to approach the Arbitrator seeking enhancement of the compensation.

In that view of the matter,
learned Counsel appearing for the respondent-NHAI submits that since the writ petition filed at the hands of the other persons standing along with the petitioner in respect of the same property has already NC: 2023:KHC:28594 been directed to be considered before the Arbitrator in the appeal that could be preferred, this writ petition may also be disposed of in similar terms.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the petitioner however, seeks to submit that there are certain issues raised by the petitioners regarding the Special Land Acquisition Officer leaving away a portion of the notified lands for determination of compensation on the ground that the same is B-kharab land and it does not belong to the petitioner.

The learned Counsel would further submit that the Special Land Acquisition Officer did not deposit the award determined by the officer in accordance with law and therefore, the Special Land Acquisition Officer should also be directed to pay the interest on the award determined and compensation payable by the authority commencing from the date of the award till payment.
4. Learned Counsel for the respondent-NHAI seeks to object to the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the petitioner.

Learned Counsel submits that the question NC: 2023:KHC:28594 as to whether the determination of the award made by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is in accordance with law or not has to be considered by the Arbitrator.
The question of payment of interest can also be addressed only in accordance with law.
Therefore, it is submitted that all questions can be left open for determination before the Arbitrator.
5. Accordingly, the writ petition stands disposed of in terms of the orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.47131/2015.
It is also made clear that all contentions are left open permitting the petitioner to urge before the Arbitrator.
